name: Veeratteswarar Temple, Tiruvirkudi
deity: Shiva as Veeratteswarar (Jalandhara Samhara Murti), with the goddess Elavar Kuzhali
tradition: Shaiva — a Paadal Petra Sthalam and one of the Ashta Veerattanam
summary: Tiruvirkudi, in the Tiruvarur country, is one of the eight Ashta Veerattanam shrines, each marking a heroic deed of Shiva. Here the lord is worshipped as Veeratteswarar, the form in which he overcame the demon Jalandhara — the episode remembered locally as Jalandhara Samharam. A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung in the Tevaram, with the goddess Elavar Kuzhali, it joins the devotional voice of the Tamil saints to one of the great mythic victories of Shaiva tradition.

sections.history: Tiruvirkudi is an old Shaiva village-temple near Nannilam, hymned in the seventh-century Tevaram and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. Its special standing comes from its place among the Ashta Veerattanam — the eight sites, each tied to one of Shiva's victories over the forces of disorder. The stone temple reflects Chola-period building; its historical name is given as Tiruvirkudi Veerattam, marking it as the veerattam, the field of valour, for the defeat of Jalandhara.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan, with a five-tiered rajagopuram, pillared halls and the sanctum of Veeratteswarar; the goddess Elavar Kuzhali has her own shrine. As a veerattanam temple, the iconography and worship keep the memory of Shiva's conquest of Jalandhara, and the form of the lord as the vanquisher of the demon is central to the sacred image the pilgrim comes to see.
sections.legends: The legend that defines Tiruvirkudi is Shiva's destruction of Jalandhara. In the traditional account the demon, grown powerful and arrogant, threatened the order of the worlds and even attempted to deceive the goddess. To end him, Shiva is said to have traced a circle that became a radiant discus, which severed the demon — a weapon later entrusted to Vishnu. The site thus became Jalandhara Samharam, and the lord is worshipped here as Jalandhara Samhara Murti, the hero of that victory.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva festival calendar — Maha Shivaratri, Pradosham, the Margazhi observances and the annual Brahmotsavam — and its identity as an Ashta Veerattanam shrine gives particular weight to the days that recall Shiva's heroic form. Pilgrims completing the circuit of the eight veerattanam temples make a point of worshipping here.
sections.experience: Tiruvirkudi is a quiet delta temple whose atmosphere is shaped by its mythic charge. Pilgrims come aware that they stand on one of the eight fields of Shiva's valour, and the darshan of Veeratteswarar carries the sense of a victory of order over chaos. For those making the Ashta Veerattanam pilgrimage, it is an essential and moving stop.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvirkudi is in Tiruvarur district, near Nannilam, roughly 20 km from Tiruvarur; the nearest rail heads are Nannilam and Tiruvarur, with local buses and taxis to the village.
